aboutGame.title: What Are Bethe Strings?
paragraphs: Bethe strings are bound-state excitations in integrable one-dimensional quantum systems. In the Bethe ansatz, their particles are described by complex rapidities arranged in regular patterns. The same framework helps explain bound clusters in attractive Bose gases and collective excitations in quantum spin chains.

Experiments probe these states through measurable signatures. Earlier magnetic-material studies detected string excitations through spectroscopy, while a 2026 Nature Communications study used an attractive one-dimensional cesium gas to investigate a mixture of different string sizes through expansion energy, momentum distributions, and correlations.

items.question: What are Bethe strings?
items.answer: Bethe strings are bound-state excitations in certain one-dimensional integrable quantum systems. Their name comes from the string-like arrangement of complex rapidities in Bethe ansatz solutions.

items.question: How do Bethe strings form in an ultracold gas?
items.answer: In the cited cesium experiment, researchers confined atoms to narrow tubes and swept their interactions from repulsive to attractive. This produced a mixture of bound clusters with different sizes.

items.question: How are Bethe strings detected?
items.answer: Researchers compare how the gas expands along its one-dimensional tubes and after release into three dimensions. Differences in release energy, together with momentum and correlation measurements, support the bound-state interpretation.

items.question: Were Bethe strings observed before the 2026 gas experiment?
items.answer: Yes. Earlier spectroscopy experiments in magnetic materials reported signatures of Bethe string excitations. The 2026 study investigated a different platform: an attractive one-dimensional Bose gas.

items.question: Are Bethe strings the strings of string theory?
items.answer: Here, a string is a pattern of rapidities describing a bound state in quantum matter. It is distinct from the fundamental strings proposed in high-energy string theory.
